ELI5: Why do different areas develop different accents?
You know the game telephone? That's why.

Disclaimer: I'm no linguist, but I've watched some documentaries and talked to enough foreigners to talk out of my ass.

I read/saw somewhere that the basics of it is that different regions develop vocables according to how the majority of people talk. If 6 out of 10 people talk in some way, by the end of the year, 9 out of those 10 will talk in an accent more close to eachother.

Personally, I think where you are from has a lot to do with it (culture, ancestors, weather). I have friends in Portugal, the U.S., Brazil, Chile, England, etc., and in my experience with languages, I haven't found a single person outside of my country that can pronounce a hard 'R'. I'm from Argentina and a lot of us say a hard R when we talk, but why others can't? Apparently some of my ancestors could, and it became so common that evolved into what it is today, that many can.

So transfer that to a region where people from different cities named A and B live very near, a lot people from A pronounce it X, and those from B pronounce it Y.

Here's a handy link I found too.

I'm really interested in languages and accents in general but I'd never become a linguist. That is why, if I'm incorrect in anything, please let me know.

We copy others with everything we do, maybe not 100% but even a small influence can effect someone greatly. If areas are isolated they talk in a group that if cut off from another group. If it just happen to turn out that a language culture forms in one that is different from the other one. This influences everyone within that group.

And if someone from another group moves in with this group, they will still be influenced. And it is dependant on how much interaction they have and how much they want to be part of the group.

For example a person who moves into an area and never talks to any of the people living there. He is unlikely to take over any of their quirks. However if you move somewhere and start working for and with them and make them your friends, they will now be part of your life and so you unconsciously urge to be like them.

An insular culture helps. Hurts? Whichever.

You really can't understand how insular the deep south in the U.S. is unless you've lived there are a northerner. Which is why, for example, the Texas accent is noticeable in Austin or Houston, but extremely pronounced in the small central counties. Areas where, if you aren't from there, they don't want you there. Areas that are largely descendant from a cultural minority that was subsumed by other cultures in Europe, interestingly enough.

I'm not an expert by any means, but what helps me is being able to tell that you're dreaming. I have to notice something that's a bit off, like putting stuff in a bag takes longer than it should, or people acting really predictable in a situation. Something that makes me stop and think "hey wait a minute, this must be a dream."

After that, I like to think of it like a video game. I usually think of the Quake console, where you press ~ to enter cheat codes, but most of the Bethesda games (Fallout, Elder Scrolls, etc.) have the same feature. Basically once I recognize I'm in a dream I mentally hit the ~ button and start typing whatever I want to do. My favorites are god mode (for me it basically works like Wolverine's regeneration powers), Rewind (go back in time and do something different), and Drop Item (think of a thing and it appears).

I've read some guides in the past and it seems like the biggest hurdle is figuring out how to let yourself know that you're dreaming. Some people use a symbol or a phrase that they would recognize as something they would only see in a dream. I don't really know what works for everyone but once you can let yourself know that you're dreaming, then you basically just come up with a system to start screwing around in your own personal sandbox.

Not sure if this helps much but hopefully it's a start.

As one post will not cover this answer completely, I will just outline the main methods here and provide some links.
There are 2 main methods - waking induced lucid dream (WILD) and dream induced lucid dream (DILD).

 

Using WILD you try to induce a lucid dream from your waking state - this is achieved by utilising sleep paralysis or hypnagogia. You basically relax until you are very tired (sport helps!) and slide into a dreaming state. More information on this technique...
DILD is often achieved by a technique called Mnemonically Induced Lucid Dream (MILD), which is a fancy name for saying that one wants to remember to check whether he is dreaming. Here is a link for that one...

 

Also: Be critical about your environment. Always ask yourself, whether you are dreaming or not (at least 5 times a day). If you do not know the answer with absolute certainty, do a reality check. Good luck!
